subject: Secure data annotations at scale
text:

Let me know if it makes sense to chat, happy to share some ideas based on how we've helped similar teams,

subject: Training data pipeline for perception model
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Mytra who was moving from simulation to real-world data collection to train their perception model. At the time they lacked a system to effectively index, auto-label and QA to keep up with the surging training data volume. I wonder if you've encountered similar challenges at [COMPANY]? 

In case Encord is new to you - we help physical AI teams (e.g. Skydio, Mytra, Fox Robotics, etc.) automate their annotation pipelines as they scale. Handful of customers in the space leverage our model-assisted workflow and our labelling editor's support across 2D (image & video) and 3D point cloud data, as a complement to Foxglove.

Keen to hear how you're thinking about your training data as you scale? I'm flexible Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to chat.

subject: Accelerating iterations for driver safety models
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Motive as they moved from frame-based to video
annotation. Like many fleet safety teams, they faced challenges around
handling billion miles of in-cab and dashcam footage, e.g. surfacing
relevant driver behaviours and maintaining temporal consistency. With
common objectives of better driver protection, have you encountered similar
bottlenecks at [COMPANY]?

In case Encord is new to you - we've built a few things that might help:

   1. Model-assisted auto-labelling to cut down repetitive frame-by-frame
   work
   2. Consolidated platform for curation + annotation to reduce tooling
   overhead
   3. Org and project-level analytics to track data quality and annotation
   efficiency

How are you approaching data preparations / model iteration at [COMPANY]? I'm
flexible Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to bouncing ideas.

subject: Spoke to [SENDER] Puleo a few months back
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Our Head of ML spoke with [SENDER] Puleo earlier this year & having also read the Content Annotations blog post, seems like it could be worth having a quick chat with the wider team.

I lead a Multimodal team here at Encord, working with several frontier teams including Thinking Machine Labs, Boston Dynamics & Wayve - helping them to drive innovation by building scalable multimodal annotation, curation, & model evaluation pipelines. 

These teams decided against continuing to build in-house - instead preferring to leverage Encord's platform to speed up annotation via pre-labelling LLMs, create flexible QA & task routing workflows to best leverage golden subject matter experts, whilst gaining full visibility into organisation-wide annotation analytics for managing HITL teams. 

Curious to know if you'd be interested in learning more about the platform?

text:

   efficiency

How are you approaching multimodal data requirements at IAS? I'm flexible
Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to bounce around some ideas.
